major2.title: Microbes in Bhartiya Gyan Parampara
major2.subtitle: Kanva, Atreya, Agastya; fermented foods; organic farming; Indian microbiologists; mushrooms.

topics.title: Kanva, Atreya, Agastya and Krimi-roga
topics.subtitle: Classical references to microbes and disease

blocks.title: Context
blocks.body: Ancient Indian medical literature refers to krimi (minute disease-causing agents) and to hygiene, fermented preparations and plant-based treatments. Kanva, Atreya and Agastya appear in the syllabus as contributors to this traditional understanding.

left.title: What to write
items: Name the seer and the context (health / food / farming)
State that krimi are minute causative agents
Do not equate them with modern bacterial taxonomy

right.title: Exam caution
right.body: Treat traditional observation and modern microbiology as historically linked, not identical systems.

blocks.body: Definition of traditional microbial knowledge → named contributors → krimi-roga idea → one modern parallel (pathogen / fermentation).

topics.title: Microbes in health: fermented foods and probiotics
topics.subtitle: Lactic fermentations in the Indian kitchen

blocks.title: Probiotics
blocks.body: Live microorganisms which, when consumed in adequate amounts, confer a health benefit on the host. Traditional fermented foods are a practical source.

blocks.title: Indian examples
items: Idli and dosa batter — mixed lactic + yeast fermentation
Beverages such as toddy in some regions

blocks.body: Define fermentation → name two foods with organisms involved → probiotic idea → one health point. Avoid medical claims.

right.title: Practices
items: Jeevamrit / panchagavya type preparations as traditional inputs

blocks.body: List 4 microbial roles in soil + 3 traditional practices + one named biofertiliser.

topics.title: Indian scientists: Iyengar, Desikachari, K.C. Mehta
topics.subtitle: Phycology and plant pathology

left.title: M.O.P. Iyengar
left.body: Father of Indian phycology; described many Indian algae and founded a school of algal research.

right.title: T.V. Desikachari
right.body: Cyanobacterial taxonomy; monographs on Indian blue-green algae.

blocks.body: K.C. Mehta is remembered for work on cereal rusts and plant pathology in India — useful when the paper links microbes to crop disease.
Table: Scientist | Field | One contribution. 5–6 lines each in a long answer.

blocks.title: Mushroom
blocks.body: Fleshy fruiting body of certain fungi, mostly Basidiomycetes. Used as food where correctly identified; many wild forms are toxic.

blocks.title: Exam points
items: Edible vs poisonous distinction is essential
Traditional use as food in several regions
Modern cultivation of Agaricus, Pleurotus, Volvariella

blocks.body: Definition → traditional use → one cultivated genus → a safety sentence.

major2.title: Virus and Prokaryotes
major2.subtitle: Viruses, TMV, bacteriophage, Mycoplasma, Archaea, Actinomycetes, bacteria and cyanobacteria.

topics.title: History and general account of viruses
topics.subtitle: Acellular obligate parasites

blocks.title: Virus
blocks.body: Acellular infectious particle with nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein coat (capsid); multiplies only inside a living host cell.

left.title: Properties
items: No cell wall, no independent metabolism

blocks.body: Definition → living/non-living debate (4 points) → structure (nucleic acid + capsid ± envelope) → example.

left.title: TMV
items: RNA virus of tobacco and related plants

right.title: Bacteriophage
items: T-even phage: head, collar, sheath, tail fibres

blocks.body: Draw TMV rod and T4 phage. Write one cycle (lytic) in 5 steps.

topics.title: Mycoplasma
topics.subtitle: Smallest free-living prokaryotes without a wall

blocks.title: Mycoplasma
blocks.body: Wall-less prokaryotes bounded by a plasma membrane; highly pleomorphic; resistant to penicillin; cause plant diseases such as little-leaf of brinjal (phytoplasma-allied group in applied papers).
3 unique characters + one plant disease + why antibiotics that target peptidoglycan fail.
Contrast table of 5 points; one economic importance each.

blocks.title: Bacteria
blocks.body: Unicellular prokaryotes with peptidoglycan wall, nucleoid, 70S ribosomes; shapes: coccus, bacillus, spirillum, vibrio.

blocks.title: Reproduction and importance
items: Binary fission; also transformation, transduction, conjugation
Nitrogen fixers, decomposers, pathogens, industry (Lactobacillus, Streptomyces)
Cyanobacteria: photosynthetic prokaryotes with chlorophyll a
Nostoc, Anabaena — heterocysts; Volvox is NOT cyanobacteria

blocks.body: Draw a bacterial cell. List 4 economic points. Separate cyanobacteria with 3 characters + 2 examples.

major2.title: Fungi
major2.subtitle: Ainsworth classification and type genera used in the paper.

blocks.title: Fungi
blocks.body: Eukaryotic, chlorophyll-less, spore-producing organisms with chitinous wall, absorptive nutrition and a mycelial thallus of hyphae.

blocks.title: Ainsworth outline (exam list)
items: Oomycota (now often Stramenopila, still in older syllabi)

blocks.body: 5 general characters + classification to class with one example each.
Define plasmogamy, karyogamy, meiosis. Map each to a class.

blocks.title: Albugo candida
blocks.body: Obligate parasite causing white rust of crucifers. Intercellular mycelium with knob-like haustoria; asexual conidia in chains under the epidermis; sexual oospores.
Host + symptoms + asexual vs sexual reproduction + a labelled diagram of a pustule.
Life-cycle diagrams. Contrast sporangiospore vs ascospore.

right.title: Imperfect fungi
items: Cercospora — leaf spots, long septate conidia
No known sexual stage in Deuteromycetes

blocks.body: Puccinia 5-spore types table. One disease each for Alternaria and Cercospora. Economic importance of fungi: food, antibiotics, disease, industry.

blocks.title: Algae
blocks.body: Simple, chlorophyll-bearing, thalloid plants, usually aquatic, without true roots, stems or leaves, reproducing by spores and gametes.
5 characters + pigments / storage / flagella table for green, brown, red.

right.title: Chara
items: Advanced green alga, often linked to land-plant ancestry

blocks.body: Draw Volvox coenobium and Chara node with sex organs.
One unique character each + one economic point for diatoms.

right.title: Polysiphonia
items: Triphasic life cycle: gametophyte, carposporophyte, tetrasporophyte

blocks.body: Name the three phases of Polysiphonia. Contrast brown vs red pigments.

blocks.title: Points
items: Agar from Gelidium / Gracilaria; algin from brown algae; carrageenan from red algae
Nitrogen fixation by Anabaena in rice fields

blocks.body: Write under Food / Industry / Agriculture / Harmful — 3 points each.

major2.title: Bryophyta
major2.subtitle: Kashyap, Ram Udar, Riccia, Marchantia, Anthoceros, Polytrichum.

blocks.title: Bryophytes
blocks.body: Avascular embryophytes, usually amphibious, with a dominant gametophyte and a dependent sporophyte. They need water for fertilisation.

left.title: Shiv Ram Kashyap
left.body: Father of Indian bryology; Himalayan liverworts.

right.title: Ram Udar
right.body: Lucknow school; taxonomy of Indian bryophytes.

blocks.body: Define + 4 characters + two Indian names with one line each.

topics.title: Life cycle and alternation of generations
topics.subtitle: Gametophyte dominant

blocks.body: Draw a labelled cycle. State which generation is photosynthetic.

left.title: Riccia
items: Sporophyte: capsule only (no foot/seta in typical accounts)

blocks.body: Compare 8 points. Draw Marchantia thallus with gemma cup.
Why Anthoceros sporophyte is considered advanced. Moss vs liverwort table.

blocks.title: Points
items: Sphagnum peat: fuel, packing, horticulture, surgical dressing
Pioneer on bare rock; soil formation
Ecological indicators of humidity and pollution

blocks.body: 5 numbered points with one example each.

major3.title: Introduction to Applied Botany
major3.subtitle: Objectives, Indian context, history, plants and human welfare.

topics.title: Objectives and importance in the Indian context
topics.subtitle: Why applied botany

blocks.title: Applied Botany
blocks.body: Use of plant science for agriculture, health, industry, environment and rural livelihood.
Definition → 5 objectives → 4 Indian examples.

topics.title: History and evolution of Botany in India
topics.subtitle: From Vrikshayurveda to BSI

items: Traditional plant science in Vedic and Ayurvedic texts
Botanical Survey of India, CSIR, ICAR
Green Revolution and modern crop science

blocks.body: Four-era timeline, one name or institution per era.

left.title: Provisioning
items: Food, fodder, fibre, fuel, medicine, timber, rubber, dyes

right.title: Regulating and cultural
items: Oxygen, carbon sink, climate, soil, water

blocks.body: Use the words food, medicine, ecology, culture — one paragraph each.

topics.title: Disciplines of Botany for human welfare
topics.subtitle: A map of applied fields

blocks.body: Six disciplines in a table: field | application | one example.
Always: definition, Indian context, 5–6 numbered applications, one limitation or future line (e.g. climate-resilient crops), conclusion.

blocks.title: Pollution
blocks.body: Undesirable change in the physical, chemical or biological characteristics of air, water, soil or space that harms living organisms.
Definition + 5 types with one source and one effect each.

blocks.title: Phytoremediation
blocks.body: Use of plants to extract, degrade, stabilise or volatilise environmental pollutants.
Define 4 modes + one plant example each.

blocks.title: Bioremediation
blocks.body: Use of living organisms, especially microbes, to detoxify pollutants.
Contrast phyto- vs bio-remediation in a 6-row table.
Green belts along roads and industries trap particulates, reduce noise and moderate temperature. Species choice: dust-tolerant, evergreen, large leaf area (e.g. Ficus, Neem, Polyalthia).
Four design rules of a green belt + four recommended trees.
End any long answer with two limitations.

major3.title: Agriculture, Horticulture and Forestry
major3.subtitle: Ancient practice to polyhouse, drip, hydroponics and silviculture.

blocks.title: Points
items: Krishi-Parashara and similar texts in the IKS frame

blocks.body: 5 practices + why they remain relevant (soil health, diversity).

left.title: Methods
items: Computer / sensor-based irrigation and climate control

blocks.body: Define each method in 2 lines with one advantage.

blocks.title: Organic farming
blocks.body: A production system that avoids synthetic fertilisers and pesticides, relying on crop rotation, organics, biofertilisers and biological control.
Principles (health, ecology, fairness, care) + 4 practices + 2 limitations (yield, certification).

Horticulture is the intensive cultivation of garden crops: pomology, olericulture, floriculture and plantation spices. In Madhya Pradesh this includes orange, tomato, chilli, coriander and ornamental nursery trade.
Definition + 4 branches + one local crop example each.

blocks.title: Silviculture
blocks.body: The theory and practice of raising and tending forest crops.

blocks.title: Exam list
items: NTFPs — tendu, mahua, lac, medicinal plants

blocks.body: Define forestry vs silviculture. Three types of agroforestry with diagrams in words.

major3.title: Ethnobotany
major3.subtitle: Rural development, ethnomedicine, fibres and food crops.

blocks.title: Channels
items: Skill in nursery and seed production

blocks.body: Five numbered rural applications with a plant name each.

blocks.title: Ethnobotany
blocks.body: The study of how people of a culture use plants for food, medicine, ritual, fibre and other needs.
For answers: record local name, botanical identity, part used, preparation and stated purpose. Do not present folk claims as proven therapy.
Definition → method of documentation → 4 examples in a table.

blocks.title: Examples
items: Banana / coconut coir in some regions
Bamboo and munj grass for baskets

blocks.body: Fibre | species | plant part | use — four rows.
Besides wheat and rice: millets (kodo, kutki, jowar), pulses, leafy amaranth, mahua flowers, ber, tendu fruit and bamboo shoots appear in central-Indian diets. Diversity is food security.
Name 6 local food plants with the edible part.
Document knowledge with community credit. Avoid biopiracy narratives in a first-year answer; stress conservation of both plants and knowledge.
One short paragraph on benefit-sharing is enough for 3-mark ethics tags.

major3.title: Biotechnology and Bioinformatics
major3.subtitle: Tissue culture, rDNA, BLAST and FASTA.

blocks.title: Plant tissue culture
blocks.body: Aseptic culture of plant cells, tissues or organs on a defined medium to regenerate plants or products.

items: Inoculation on MS medium with auxin/cytokinin

blocks.body: Totipotency definition + 5 steps + two applications (micropropagation, virus-free plants).

topics.title: Recombinant DNA technique
topics.subtitle: The idea, not the full protocol

blocks.title: rDNA
blocks.body: Joining DNA from different sources using restriction enzymes and ligase, then propagating it in a host (usually E. coli) with a vector (plasmid).

blocks.title: Plant examples at idea level
items: Golden rice as a biofortification example (policy debates exist; state the science only)

blocks.body: Tools: restriction enzyme, vector, ligase, host. One crop example.

blocks.title: Bioinformatics
blocks.body: Use of computation to store, retrieve and analyse biological data, especially sequences.
Definition + 3 databases + 2 tools.

left.title: BLAST
left.body: Basic Local Alignment Search Tool. Finds local similarity of a query sequence against a database. Programmes: blastn, blastp, blastx.

right.title: FASTA
right.body: Both a sequence format (header starting with >) and a fast alignment algorithm by Pearson. Used for pairwise similarity.

blocks.body: Expand both abbreviations. One sentence on when a botanist uses them (identify an unknown ITS/rbcL sequence).
Five applied points, no software screenshots needed.

minor1.title: Plants in Bhartiya Gyan Parampara
minor1.subtitle: Definition of botany, Indian history, Vedas, Rishis, traditional food and medicine.

topics.title: Definition, scope and importance of Botany
topics.subtitle: Plant biology

blocks.title: Botany
blocks.body: Scientific study of plants — structure, function, classification, ecology, genetics and uses.
Definition → 5 branches → 5 importance points.

items: ICAR, CSIR, Green Revolution, J.C. Bose

blocks.body: Four periods, one fact each.
Rigveda groups plants as trees (vriksha), herbs (oshadhi) and climbers (virudh). Atharvaveda is rich in medicinal (bheshaj) plants. Use these four terms in the answer.
Name the four Vedic plant groups with one example if taught in class.

topics.title: Parashar, Charak, Sushrut
topics.subtitle: Three names the paper always asks

left.title: Parashar
left.body: Vrikshayurveda — plant life, soil, disease of trees.

right.title: Charak & Sushrut
right.body: Charaka Samhita: Dravyaguna, medicinal groups. Sushruta: plant drugs and surgical materials.

blocks.body: Table of 3 scholars × text × contribution.
Six-row table: common | scientific | part | traditional use. Add a caution line.

minor1.title: Plant Morphology
minor1.subtitle: Root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit and seed.

blocks.body: Draw the three storage shapes. Two-line function of root: absorption + anchorage.
How to tell a stem: nodes, internodes, scale leaves, buds — even when underground.
Define phyllotaxy. Draw palmate vs pinnate.

blocks.title: Flower
blocks.body: A condensed shoot meant for sexual reproduction in angiosperms.

blocks.title: Must-list
items: Placentation: marginal, axile, parietal, free-central, basal

blocks.body: Define actinomorphic/zygomorphic. One example each for three ovary positions.
State the two developmental rules. Draw a dicot seed.

minor1.title: Plant Anatomy
minor1.subtitle: Cell, tissues, root, stem and leaf.

blocks.title: Plant cell
blocks.body: Eukaryotic cell with a cellulose wall, large vacuole and plastids — characters that separate it from a typical animal cell.
Draw a labelled plant cell. Three differences vs animal cell.
Table of simple tissues: living/dead, wall, function, position.
Two labelled T.S. diagrams. Casparian strips in endodermis.

left.title: Dicot stem
items: Open collateral bundles in a ring

blocks.body: How to identify the slide in practicals: bundle arrangement.

Dicot dorsiventral leaf: upper palisade, lower spongy mesophyll, stomata mainly below. Monocot isobilateral: similar mesophyll both sides, parallel veins, stomata on both surfaces. Kranz anatomy in C4 leaves (bundle sheath chloroplasts).
Draw dicot leaf T.S. with stomata, palisade, vein.

left.title: Terms
items: Imbibition — water into hydrophilic colloids (seed coat, wood)
Diffusion — net movement down a gradient
Osmosis — water across a semipermeable membrane

blocks.body: Define all four terms. One example each.
Name the theory of ascent of sap accepted in class and 3 supporting points.

blocks.title: Mass flow / pressure flow (Münch)
blocks.body: Sugars loaded into phloem at source raise ψs, water enters, turgor pushes sap to the sink where sugar is unloaded.
Source vs sink examples. Why phloem is living tissue.

blocks.title: Photosynthesis
blocks.body: Formation of organic compounds from CO2 and water using light, releasing O2, in chloroplasts.
Equation. Two reactions. One difference C3/C4.

blocks.title: Respiration
blocks.body: Oxidation of organic food to release energy as ATP.

blocks.title: Stages
items: Electron transport — cristae,  O2 is the acceptor

blocks.body: Equation of aerobic respiration. Net ATP at first-year level as taught (often 36/38 — write what the class notes say).

minor1.title: Reproduction, Growth and Propagation
minor1.subtitle: Propagules, sexual/asexual, PGRs, gametophyte, sporophyte, AOG.

blocks.body: Define vegetative propagation. Four natural + two artificial methods.

left.title: Asexual
items: Useful to keep a variety true

blocks.body: Define double fertilisation in 3 lines (syngamy + triple fusion).

blocks.title: One function each
items: Auxin — apical dominance, rooting of cuttings
Cytokinin — cell division, delay of senescence

blocks.body: Elicitors are molecules that trigger defence or secondary-metabolite pathways (jasmonate, salicylic acid, pathogen fragments). Mention if the long-answer tag includes elicitors.
Table of 5 hormones × 2 functions. One agricultural use each.

left.title: Gametophyte (n)
left.body: Produces gametes by mitosis. Dominant in bryophytes.

right.title: Sporophyte (2n)
right.body: Produces spores by meiosis. Dominant in vascular plants.

blocks.body: State the chromosome number of each. One example group each.
A haploid gametophyte alternates with a diploid sporophyte in the life cycle. Fusion of gametes restores 2n; meiosis in the sporophyte restores n. Homospory vs heterospory may be asked in one line.
Draw the cycle with n / 2n labels. Write ‘isomorphic’ vs ‘heteromorphic’ with one algal and one land-plant example.

minor2.title: Plants in Indian Knowledge Systems
minor2.subtitle: Iyengar, Kashyap, S.S. Bir, Birbal Sahni, D.D. Pant.

blocks.body: Iyengar founded modern Indian phycology, described numerous taxa and trained a school of algal taxonomists. Mention green algae of Indian waters in the same paragraph.
One paragraph + why algal survey matters (food, agar, blooms).
Called the father of Indian bryology. Worked especially on liverworts of the Himalaya. Pair with Ram Udar if a 5-mark asks ‘Indian bryologists’.
Name + field + one region of work.
S.S. Bir contributed to the taxonomy and cytology of Indian pteridophytes. Useful when the paper asks for an Indian pteridologist.
One named Indian pteridologist is enough if you add two fern examples (Dryopteris, Adiantum, Lycopodium).

topics.title: Birbal Sahni and D.D. Pant — gymnosperms
topics.subtitle: Fossil and living gymnosperms

left.title: Birbal Sahni
left.body: Pioneer of Indian palaeobotany; Birbal Sahni Institute, Lucknow; fossil plants of the Gondwana.

blocks.body: Two names, two contributions, one institute.
Ancient texts distinguish herbs, trees, climbers and aquatic plants and record sacred groves and medicinal groups. Use this as a 3-mark opener, then move to modern classification.
Do not invent Sanskrit quotations. Name Vanaspati / Oshadhi / Vriksha.

blocks.title: Algae
blocks.body: Chlorophyllous thallophytes, mostly aquatic.
5 characters + 4 economic uses.
Spherical colony of biflagellate cells in a mucilage matrix. Posterior cells may form oogonia and antheridia. Daughter colonies invert and release. Exam diagram is mandatory.
Label: vegetative cell, daughter colony, egg, antheridium.
Economic: penicillin, yeast, mushrooms, plant disease, mycorrhiza — one line each.
Draw asexual and sexual stages side by side.
Table: nutrition, pigment, wall, habitat, example. Five rows. Favourite 5-mark.
Three classes with one example each.
Dorsiventral thallus, rhizoids and scales, air pores, gemma cups, erect antheridiophores and archegoniophores, sporophyte with foot, seta and capsule with elaters.
Asexual gemmae + sexual cycle. Draw gemma cup.

blocks.title: Pteridophytes
blocks.body: Vascular cryptogams with independent sporophyte, true roots/stems/leaves, and usually homosporous or heterosporous life cycles. No seeds.
5 characters + 4 uses.
Creeping or erect sporophyte, microphylls, protostele, strobili of sporophylls, homosporous, photosynthetic gametophyte in many species. Practical: T.S. stem and strobilus.
Morphology + anatomy + reproduction, 5 lines each.
Rows: dominant generation, vascular tissue, true roots, seed, examples. Leave no cell blank.

blocks.title: Gymnosperms
blocks.body: Seed plants with naked ovules, not enclosed in an ovary; often woody; no true fruits or flowers.
5 characters + 4 classes with examples.
Why Cycas is a living fossil. Draw a megasporophyll.
Tall tree, dwarf shoots with needles, mycorrhizal roots, monoecious, winged pollen, ovuliferous scales, naked seeds. Secondary wood with tracheids and resin canals.
Male vs female cone. T.S. needle — a practical favourite.

blocks.title: Points
items: Seeds of chilgoza pine as food

blocks.body: Five numbered uses with a genus each.
Table: ovule, fruit, flower, vessels, double fertilisation, examples.
Write one mock description of a mustard or china-rose flower as practice.

Bentham and Hooker divided seed plants into Dicotyledons (Polypetalae, Gamopetalae, Monochlamydeae), Gymnosperms and Monocotyledons. It is a practical system used in Indian herbaria, not phylogenetic APG.
Three dicot series + position of gymnosperms + one limitation (not evolutionary).

blocks.title: Malvaceae
blocks.body: Mostly herbs/shrubs; mucilage; alternate palmate leaves; epicalyx often present; twisted corolla; monadelphous stamens; axile placentation; capsule or schizocarp. Examples: Hibiscus, Gossypium, Abelmoschus.
Floral formula of Hibiscus. Five diagnostic characters. Economic: cotton, okra, ornamentals.

blocks.title: Poaceae
blocks.body: Monocot herbs; hollow internodes; ligulate leaves; spikelet inflorescence with glumes, lemma, palea; lodicules; 3 stamens; superior ovary with two feathery stigmas; caryopsis.
Draw a spikelet. Economic: rice, wheat, maize, sugarcane, bamboo.
Habit, leaf, inflorescence, androecium, fruit, examples — six rows.
